Gap junctions are intercellular channels that allow direct passage of small molecules and ions (typically < 1,000–1,500 Da) between adjacent cells.  
A 1,000-dalton fluorescent molecule fits this size limit.  
Desmosomes (spot or belt) provide adhesion but not molecular passage.  
Tight junctions seal intercellular spaces, blocking movement of substances between cells.  

Final answer: (C)
